expected.notes: Test 2 (out-of-bounds read): CBMC reports "dereference failure: pointer outside object bounds in values[index]" (array_lookup.pointer_dereference, src/array_lookup.c:9) with a counterexample where index == count (e.g. count = 6, index = 6), plus the harness postconditions rc == ARRAY_LOOKUP_ERR_RANGE and *out unchanged. ASan reports heap-buffer-overflow at src/array_lookup.c:9 in the trusted index_equals_count test. The Clang Static Analyzer has no finding (array size unknown to it). The sanitizer gate also fails (RUNTIME_TEST_FAILED), but COUNTEREXAMPLE_FOUND ranks worse.

mul_u64_checked is correct: it compiles cleanly, has no analyzer findings and passes the trusted tests under ASan/UBSan/LSan. The harness compares it with the exact 128-bit product for two unconstrained uint64_t inputs; deciding that the 64-bit division UINT64_MAX / a agrees with a 128-bit multiplication is a very hard SAT problem: raw `timeout 25 cbmc ...` (same flags as Lean C) is killed after 25 s without a verdict. With verification.timeout_s: 3 Lean C reports TIMEOUT -- passing tests are not promoted to a verification result, and the repair agent is not invoked.

Test 3 (division by zero, then a NEW counterexample): on the shipped code CBMC reports both safe_ratio.division-by-zero (den = 0) and safe_ratio.overflow "arithmetic overflow on signed division" (num = INT_MIN, den = -1) on the same division (src/safe_ratio.c:8); UBSan aborts the zero_den and int_min_by_minus_one tests. Mock round 1 adds only the den == 0 check: the division-by-zero failures disappear while the overflow failure (same property, same line) remains, so the round is a strict improvement and is accepted. Mock round 2 also rejects INT_MIN / -1 and the result is VERIFIED_BOUNDED. No Clang Static Analyzer finding (den is not known to be 0 on any path).

Test 4 (signed overflow): CBMC's mandatory --signed-overflow-check reports "arithmetic overflow on signed + in a + b" (checked_add.overflow, src/checked_add.c:10). All harness postconditions hold under CBMC's wrap-around model, so ONLY the UB check catches the defect: the after-the-fact test is too late. UBSan aborts the positive_overflow / negative_overflow tests ("signed integer overflow: 2147483647 + 1"). No Clang Static Analyzer finding.

Test 6 (insufficient unwinding): sum_array is correct, compiles cleanly, has no analyzer findings and passes the trusted tests under ASan/UBSan/LSan, but the harness explores n <= 16 while the spec's unwind bound is 5. CBMC reports the unwinding assertion sum_array.unwind.0 as FAILED, so "no counterexample" would only cover n <= 4: Lean C reports UNKNOWN, never VERIFIED_BOUNDED. The fix is a human decision (a new, separately approved spec): spec_full_unwind.yaml (unwind 17) => VERIFIED_BOUNDED.

Test 5 (NULL dereference): the Clang Static Analyzer reports core.NullDereference "Access to field 'enabled' results in a dereference of a null pointer (loaded from variable 's')" (src/sensor.c:14, STATIC_ANALYSIS_WARNING, policy=block); CBMC reports "dereference failure: pointer NULL in s->enabled" (and s->value) with s == NULL, out != NULL; UBSan aborts the null_sensor test with "member access within null pointer of type 'const struct sensor'". Overall status is the worst gate: COUNTEREXAMPLE_FOUND.

Multi-file project: two editable sources (src/ring.c, src/ring_stats.c) sharing one protected header. Both files compile cleanly and have no analyzer findings; the trusted tests (incl. many wraparounds on exactly-sized heap storage) pass under ASan/UBSan/LSan; CBMC explores every sequence of 5 nondeterministic push/pop operations on capacities 1..3 (plus rejected capacities 0 and > RING_MAX_CAPACITY), checking the representation invariant, FIFO order and all observers against a model, with all 8 probes reachable (incl. "wrapped" and "push_full") => VERIFIED_BOUNDED.

The shipped join_with_sep stores its malloc'd buffer in res->data and, on the JOIN_ERR_FIELD error path, clears res->data without freeing it. The pointer escapes through the out-parameter, so the Clang Static Analyzer reports nothing; the spec's CBMC checks (no memory-leak check) pass with all probes reachable; the trusted tests separator_in_field and nul_in_field fail under LeakSanitizer ("Direct leak of 6 byte(s) ... allocated from join_with_sep src/join.c:22"). Overall RUNTIME_TEST_FAILED. Mock round-1 adds free(res->data) in the shared error path => VERIFIED_BOUNDED.

Test 1 (correct program): compiles cleanly, no analyzer findings, trusted tests pass under ASan/UBSan/LSan, CBMC finds no violation for len <= 8 and any idx (all loops unwound, all LEANC_REACH probes reachable) => VERIFIED_BOUNDED (never PROVED).

The shipped array_read accepts idx == len (reads one past the end). The approved harness contains two assumptions that contradict each other (len >= 8 and len <= 4), so no execution reaches the call and plain `cbmc` prints "VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL". Lean C re-runs CBMC with -DLEANC_VACUITY_CHECK: the probes after_call / null_input / out_of_range / in_range all "hold" (= unreachable), so the result is UNKNOWN (vacuous), never VERIFIED_BOUNDED. With the corrected harness (spec_fixed_harness.yaml) CBMC finds the counterexample len=4, idx=4 (pointer outside object bounds in arr[idx], src/array_read.c:11).
